text: At first Zik tried to make sense of them, searching for some order in the endless rows of glass. The labels suggested one existed. Every jar bore the same careful hand, each line etched into the base with deliberate precision. Subject. Variant. Outcome. Occasionally a number. Occasionally a single word. Whatever system governed the collection had never been intended for visitors. It assumed the reader already understood the rules.
speaker: Narrator

text: The jars themselves refused explanation.

text: One contained nothing but a chair beneath a narrow window. Dust drifted lazily through a shaft of afternoon light that never changed, though no breeze stirred it. Another held a child carefully stacking smooth black stones into a tower that collapsed each time the last piece was set in place. The child never showed frustration. He simply began again, every movement identical to the last. Farther along, a woman sat before a table covered in maps, crossing out one route after another until the parchment itself disappeared beneath the ink.
